gaps.question: What total return does a nominator actually earn on staked micro-cap alpha (price, plus nominator dividends, minus take, minus dilution), and how and when is it credited? Where can the backtester get historical per-subnet, per-validator nominator yield?
gaps.why_it_matters: All the factor evidence is price-only and gross: Maymin, plus the D6/D7 replication of SMB −0.56%/day and WML7 in the gate era. The one yield figure in the corpus (A10, ~89%/yr alpha APR on SN92) is a rough derivation, and it uses AlphaOut as the staked base even though AlphaOut includes protocol alpha. Dividends of ~0.2%/day on micro caps would be the same size as the measured size-premium reversal, so leaving them out can flip the sign of the strategy. Three points are still unverified: (a) whether stake on a hotkey without a validator permit earns zero (B18 is an inference); (b) how spec-475 Null consensus changes nominator yield (code has skip_zero_dividends, so zero-dividend hotkeys get nothing); (c) how to pick validators, given that unconfigured hotkeys default to the 18% take. Partial resolution from my read of run_coinbase.rs on main: nominator dividends are credited pro rata through increase_stake_for_hotkey_on_subnet at the epoch drain. The drain uses should_run_epoch_with_tempo (tempo 360) and can be deferred by MaxEpochsPerBlock or PendingEpochAt. That file has no stake-age or hold-period gate; I did not check the internals of increase_stake_for_hotkey_on_subnet. So the backtester should credit dividends as lumps at drain blocks, and live stake earns from the very next drain.
gaps.suggested_sources: run_coinbase.rs (drain_pending, distribute_dividends_and_incentives, calculate_dividend_distribution); stake_utils.rs (share-pool math in increase_stake_for_hotkey_on_subnet, plus the AlphaV2 storage change at v473); the Null-consensus epoch code (docs/guides/null-consensus.mdx); archive replay of TotalHotkeyAlpha/TotalHotkeyShares per (hotkey, netuid) to build share-price series; Taostats /v1/validators/yield and /v1/validators/{hotkey}/history; StakeInfoRuntimeApi at historical block hashes; a testnet experiment on dividend crediting timing.

gaps.question: How much root-dividend alpha does the beta-basket escrow hold in each micro-cap subnet, and when is it released (staker claims, validator swap_basket, dust folding, sale through the AMM before dissolution)?
gaps.why_it_matters: I checked basket_flush.rs on main. Since v441 (block 8,765,683), root dividends are credited in place on their origin subnet ('no swap runs ... zero trades on a dividend'), and holdings change only through swap_basket. That refutes D17's claim that Curated Beta creates buy flow into micro caps the validators choose. The flow scales with root_alpha ≈ rp × 0.5 × 0.82 × alpha_out. rp is about 0.48 on micro caps and about 0.14 on large caps, so roughly 20% of a micro cap's 7,200 alpha/day may have gone into the escrow whenever Σ EMA > 1. Rough derived estimate for SN92: about 0.197 alpha/block × ~475k blocks ≈ 9×10^4 alpha before claims and take, against an AlphaIn of about 435k. If that were sold at once, the price would fall by roughly 30%. This latent sell overhang is released lumpily: claims sell a pro-rata slice of every holding, validators trade through swap_basket, and on dissolution it is sold first, which drains the TAO pot before holders are paid. None of it is quantified in the corpus. Exit, sizing and dereg-loss models all depend on it.
gaps.suggested_sources: StakeInfoRuntimeApi_get_stake_info_for_coldkey(get_beta_escrow_account_id()); BetaBasketRuntimeApi get_validator_basket and get_validator_basket_nav for every root validator; PendingBasketDeposits and RootClaimableThreshold storage; root-claim and swap_basket events since block 8,765,683; claim_root.rs, basket_flush.rs and swap_basket source; a history of the root sell flag (Σ SubnetMovingPrice > 1).

gapfill.question: What total return does a nominator actually earn on staked micro-cap alpha (price, plus nominator dividends, minus take, minus dilution), and how and when is it credited? Where can the backtester get historical per-subnet, per-validator nominator yield?
gapfill.answer:
SHORT ANSWER
- The total return in TAO for a staked position on (hotkey h, subnet n), with no trades in between, is:
  1+R = (P_t1/P_t0) × (I_t1/I_t0), minus swap fees and slippage.
  - I_{h,n} = TotalHotkeyAlpha(h,n) / TotalHotkeyShares(h,n) is the hotkey's alpha share price.
  - I rises only at epoch drains, by the nominator dividend. That dividend is already net of the validator take, any childkey take and CKBurn, and it compounds automatically in alpha.
  - Dilution from alpha_out is already inside P, and inside the falling per-unit yield as stake grows. Do not subtract it a second time.
- Live measurement on 2026-10-08 (Finney spec 475, block ~9,240,8xx), net of take:
  - Micro caps: about 0.3 to 0.6%/day.
  - Largest caps: about 0.08 to 0.11%/day.
  - The yield spread (small minus big) is about +0.2 to +0.5%/day. That is the same order as the price-only SMB of −0.56%/day, so leaving yield out can flip the sign.

1) EMISSION MATH (tag v475 = what is live on Finney; RaoFoundation/subtensor, formerly opentensor/subtensor)

Per block (emit_to_subnets):
- alpha_out = get_block_emission_for_issuance(alpha_issuance). This is 1 alpha per block until a subnet's alpha issuance reaches 10.5M, then 0.5. No subnet has reached it yet; the maximum is about 6.3M.
- alpha_issuance = SubnetAlphaIn + SubnetAlphaOut + reservoir.
- Owner cut is 18% (11796/65535). Call the remainder R = 0.82 × alpha_out.
- Miners get 0.5 × R.
- Root gets root_alpha = 0.5 × R × rp.
- PendingValidatorEmission increases by 0.5 × R × (1 − rp).
- rp = root_proportion = SubnetTAO(0)·w / (SubnetTAO(0)·w + alpha_issuance).
- w = TaoWeight = 0.18. I read 0.18 on chain at blocks 4.925M, 5.5M, 6.5M, 7.5M, 8.5M and at head.
- Taoflow and the emission gate change only the TAO side, not alpha_out.
- Micro caps have a high rp: 0.48 to 0.88. Large caps are about 0.13.

At the epoch (`distribute_emission`):
1. If total miner incentive is zero, validators also receive the server (miner) alpha.
2. Each UID's dividend goes through `get_parent_child_dividends_distribution`:
   - It is split to parents by contribution: α_p·prop + w·τ_p·prop.
   - For a parent under a different coldkey, CKBurn (now 0) and the child's ChildkeyTake (0 to 18%, default 0) are deducted.
3. `calculate_dividend_distribution` takes the alpha part as d·α_h/(α_h + w·τ_h), using h's own stake. It then normalises: prop_alpha_h = PendingValidatorAlpha × alpha_div_h / Σ alpha_div.
4. `distribute_dividends_and_incentives`:
   - take = Delegates(h)/65535 × prop_alpha. It is credited as new shares to the owner coldkey at the current price, which leaves I unchanged.
   - The rest goes through `increase_stake_for_hotkey_on_subnet`, which calls `SharePool.update_value_for_all`: TotalHotkeyAlpha increases and shares do not change. Every coldkey's value floor(V·S/D) rises pro rata.
   - If the pool has no members, the amount goes to the hotkey owner instead.
   - AlphaDividendsPerSubnet(n,h) is cleared and set to the post-take nominator alpha.
   - TotalHotkeyAlphaLastEpoch(h,n) is set to the post-credit value.
   - In v475 nothing else updates the pool as a whole. The only callers of `update_value_for_all` are this credit and the unused decrease function.
   - The root portion goes to the root validator baskets (root stakers), never to alpha nominators.

Closed form:
- Gross yield per alpha per day ≈ 7200 × E × 0.82 × 0.5 × (1 − rp) / A_earn = 2952 × (1 − rp) / A_earn.
- Net yield = gross × (1 − take_h) × (1 − ck_take) × (1 − CKBurn).
- A_earn = Σ TotalHotkeyAlpha over the dividend recipients. It is not AlphaOut: AlphaOut includes burned alpha (`burn_subnet_alpha` does not reduce SubnetAlphaOut), SubnetProtocolAlpha and stake that earns nothing.
  - SN92: AlphaOut 630,980 versus A_earn 343,198. So A10 understates the yield by about 1.8×.
- Live validation:

| Subnet | rp | A_earn | Predicted gross %/day | Observed (take-0 hotkey) %/day |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SN70 | 0.655 | 182,839 | 0.557 | 0.557 |
| SN92 | 0.479 | 343,198 | 0.448 | 0.448 |
| SN64 | 0.133 | 2,789,195 | 0.0918 | 0.092 |

- Other gross yields per day: SN36 0.63%, SN16 0.32%, SN99 0.44%, SN47 0.24%, SN51 0.094%, SN4 0.089%, SN9 0.10%, SN3 0.118%, SN8 0.115%, SN1 0.16%.
- Net, stake-weighted, per day: SN64 0.084%, SN51 0.084%, SN4 0.080%, SN47 0.205%, SN57 0.303%.

2) WHEN IT IS CREDITED (verified on chain)
- The call chain is on_initialize → block_step → run_coinbase → drain_pending → distribute.
- An epoch fires when any of these holds:
  - LastEpochBlock + tempo has been reached (the stateful scheduler has period = tempo, 360 by default);
  - PendingEpochAt (a manual trigger by the subnet owner) has been reached;
  - BlocksSinceLastStep > tempo.
- Timing irregularities:
  - MaxEpochsPerBlock = 2 (1 when a Null epoch is due) defers extra epochs by one block.
  - EpochSkipped keeps the pending emission, so the next lump is doubled.
  - Non-360 tempos exist: SN1 99, SN18 1800, SN19 7200, SN38 1440.
- There is no stake-age or hold gate anywhere. `stake_into_subnet` has none. `validate_remove_stake` only checks conviction locks, collateral and the root unlock interval.
- Stake included in a block at or before B−1 earns the full drain at block B, pro rata. Stake added during block B itself does not, because B's drain runs before extrinsics. Unstaking in block B keeps the credit.
- Chain check on SN70, hotkey 56a9aee6…:

| Block | Share price | Note |
|---|---|---|
| 9,240,222 to 9,240,581 | 1.630905371 (flat) | A stake add at 9,240,223 raised TotalHotkeyAlpha but not the price |
| 9,240,582 (= LastEpochBlock) | 1.631359787 | +0.0279%, 360 blocks after the previous drain |

- Caveat: under classic Yuma (Yuma3On is at default/off on the subnets checked), a UID's dividend share follows a bond EMA (alpha = 0.1), so new stake into a validator dilutes its existing nominators for a while. On micro caps most stake is on childkey parents, and parents are paid by current contribution, which is immediate.

3) THE THREE OPEN POINTS
(a) Hotkeys without a permit:
- Under Yuma, only UIDs that hold the previous epoch's ValidatorPermit and are active earn dividends.
  - Permits go to the top MaxAllowedValidators = 64 by stake weight, with stake at least StakeThreshold = 1000. The owner UID is always permitted.
  - "Active" means weights set within activity_cutoff; earnings then come through bonds.
- So a UID without a permit earns 0 itself. But parent hotkeys earn through childkey links whether or not they are registered or permitted.
- Live data:
  - SN70: 13 UIDs, 3 permits, 49 dividend recipients, of which 46 are unregistered parents. These are root validators auto-childkeyed at proportion 1.0 to the owner hotkey (uid 0) and to hotkey 56a9 (uid 1).
  - SN92: 256 UIDs, 5 permits, 52 recipients, of which 7 are registered.
- The rule: stake earns if and only if its hotkey is a key of AlphaDividendsPerSubnet(n, ·). B18 is wrong as a blanket statement.
- Edge case: if no weights are valid (emission_sum == 0), Yuma pays in proportion to active stake.

(b) Null consensus:
- It was added in v475 (released 2026-10-07). At block 9,240,814, 0 of 128 subnets use it.
- One permit holder (the largest stake) only sets the miner weights.
- Half of the epoch budget is split in proportion to the total inherited stake weight of every registered UID with positive stake. There is no permit, activity, StakeThreshold or bond requirement. Parents still receive their split.
- `skip_zero_dividends` only skips UIDs whose payout is zero, which means zero stake. It does not cut off any staked hotkey.
- Result: the gross yield per alpha becomes uniform, V divided by the registered plus parent alpha. Net yield differs only by take.
- Unregistered hotkeys that are not parents still earn 0.

(c) Choosing a validator:
- Take is one value per hotkey for all subnets: Delegates, a PerU16 with default 11796 = 18% and MaxDelegateTake of 18%. It can be decreased at any time; increases are limited to one per 216,000 blocks.
- Gross yield per unit is nearly identical across recipients on a subnet. Take decides the net:
  - SN70, take 0: 0.0279% per epoch.
  - SN70, take 0.09: 0.0254% per epoch (= 0.0279 × 0.91).
- Rule for picking:
  - Among the AlphaDividendsPerSubnet keys, choose the hotkey with the highest trailing realised Δln I (using past data only).
  - Prefer take 0.
  - Check the child's ChildkeyTake.
  - Check that the parent link is stable (child changes take effect after a 7,200-block cooldown).

4) HISTORICAL DATA SOURCES
(i) Archive node. Run your own (about 3.5 TB or more) or use the public wss://archive.chain.opentensor.ai:443. The public node returned error −32004 "Historical work rate limit exceeded" after roughly 100 historical reads.

Storage items (all in SubtensorModule):

| Item | Keys (hashers) | Value / notes |
|---|---|---|
| TotalHotkeyAlpha | hotkey (Blake2_128Concat), netuid u16 (Identity) | u64 rao |
| TotalHotkeyShares | hotkey, netuid | U64F64; read bits/2^64. Removed from metadata at v473 |
| TotalHotkeySharesV2 | hotkey, netuid | SafeFloat {mantissa u128, exponent i64} = m·10^e; present by v411 at the latest |
| AlphaDividendsPerSubnet | netuid (Identity), hotkey (Blake2_128Concat) | Last epoch's post-take nominator alpha; meaning unchanged since v2.0.0 / spec 233, the dTAO launch |
| TotalHotkeyAlphaLastEpoch | hotkey, netuid | Post-credit value |
| LastEpochBlock, SubnetEpochIndex | netuid | Epoch timing |
| Delegates | hotkey | Take |
| ChildkeyTake | hotkey, netuid | Child take |
| ParentKeys / ChildKeys | hotkey, netuid | Vec<(u64 proportion, AccountId)> |
| RootProp | netuid | U96F32, bits/2^32. Reads 0 at block 6.5M, so compute rp yourself for older blocks |

gapfill.question: How much root-dividend alpha does the beta-basket escrow hold in each micro-cap subnet, and when is it released (staker claims, validator swap_basket, dust folding, sale through the AMM before dissolution)?
gapfill.answer:
SHORT ANSWER. Public sources do answer this. I read it directly from the chain (finney, spec 475, blocks about 9,240,000 to 9,240,920, 2026-10-08) and checked it against main of the subtensor repo. Note that github.com/opentensor/subtensor now redirects to RaoFoundation/subtensor.

Network-wide:
- The escrow (`get_beta_escrow_account_id()`, raw bytes "modl"+"subtensr"+"beta/esc" padded with zeros to 32 bytes) holds positions for 189 validator funds.
- Total NAV is 28,425 τ realizable and 28,619 τ at spot. The root cash slot is 256 τ.
- Lifetime counters: 55,681 τ deposited and 26,255 τ redeemed.
- On micro caps the escrow is a large share of the pool's alpha. For the smallest third of subnets by market cap, the median escrow is 5.3% of the pool's alpha reserve (SubnetAlphaIn) and a one-shot sale would cut the price by 9.7%. For the middle third it is 0.65% (1.3% price cut) and for the top third 1.1% (2.2%).
- This stock is not latent. Staker claims release it continuously at about 2% of each holding per day, with bursts of about 4–5% per day. Validator trades (swap_basket) cannot dump it because of price bands. It is sold all at once only when the subnet is dissolved, and SN92 is the current `get_subnet_to_prune()` result.

1) MECHANISM (code on main; pallets/subtensor/src):
- **Inflow formula** (`coinbase/run_coinbase.rs::emit_to_subnets`): root_alpha per block = RootProp × alpha_out_after_owner_cut × 0.5. The owner cut is 18%, so this is RootProp × 0.5 × 0.82 × alpha_emission.
  - RootProp = SubnetTAO[root] × TaoWeight / (that + alpha_issuance(netuid)), from `block_step.rs::root_proportion`. TaoWeight is currently 0.18.
  - RootProp therefore depends on a subnet's age (alpha issuance), not its market cap. Young micro caps have RootProp 0.3–0.88; old micro caps sit around 0.14, the same as large caps.
- **Root sell flag**: root alpha accrues only when Σ SubnetMovingPrice over emitting subnets > 1; otherwise it is recycled.
  - I sampled the sum every 3 days since v441: it ranged from 1.163 to 1.333 and is 1.186 now, so the flag has always been on.
  - The trend is down. If the sum falls to 1 or below, inflow to the escrow stops but the existing stock stays.
- **Distribution to validators** (`distribute_dividends_and_incentives`): each root-registered hotkey's take goes to the validator owner as ordinary, liquid alpha. The rest goes through `enqueue_basket_deposit` into PendingBasketDeposits.
- **In-place credit**: `basket_flush.rs::try_accumulate_basket_credit` credits the alpha to the escrow position (validator_hotkey, escrow, origin_netuid) with no swap.
  - The queue drains one hotkey per block, and also flushes immediately whenever a claim, deposit, trade or root stake change touches that fund.
  - Live queue: 2,178 rows worth about 1.9 τ in total (SN92: about 4 α), so it is immaterial.
- **Measured current inflow, net of take** (from RootAlphaDividendsPerSubnet over the last epoch, tempo 360). Effective take on SN92 is about 9%.

  | Subnet | α/block | α/day |
  |---|---|---|
  | SN92 | 0.1786 | 1,286 |
  | SN103 | 0.232 | 1,670 |
  | SN76 | 0.302 | 2,175 |
  | SN108 | 0.328 | 2,359 |
  | Large caps SN4/51/64 | about 0.05 | about 360 |
  | All subnets combined | 11.27 | — |

- **Compounding**: escrow positions are ordinary nominator stake on the validator hotkey, so they also earn that validator's alpha dividends.
- **Timeline** (upgrade blocks found by binary search on the archive node):
  - v441 (Root Reborn, accumulate in place): block 8,765,683, 2026-08-03.
  - spec 450 ("Curated Beta", `set_root_weights` live): block 8,938,465, 2026-08-27. During this window, funds that had set a weight vector sold their dividend once and re-bought across the vector.
  - spec 464 (contains the v461 changes; v461 itself was never deployed, mainnet went 459 → 464): block 9,088,597, 2026-09-17. Root weights removed; dividends accumulate in place only.
  - BasketTradingEnabled flipped to true at block 9,117,749, 2026-09-21.
  - Only 20–21 root validators ever set vectors, and they weighted large caps (SN120, 51, 4, 53, 64, 44, 3, 28, 68, 75, 93). The unweighted sum of normalized weights on micro caps was close to 0. So D17's "curated buy flow into micro caps" was weak even inside that window and has been gone since block 9,088,597. During the window, SN92's escrow went flat (35.1k → 40.2k α over 150k blocks), consistent with curated funds selling their SN92 dividends.
- **Correction to your premise**: swap_basket is the only thing that changes a fund's composition on purpose, but the escrow's quantities also change through:
  - claims, which sell a pro-rata slice;
  - dust consolidation, which sells;
  - `stake_into_basket` / `btcli root allocate`, which BUY every holding in proportion to its share of NAV;
  - compounding dividends;
  - dissolution conversion;
  - terminal write-offs (`burn_subnet_alpha`).

2) LIVE HOLDINGS (aggregate escrow alpha E, from `BetaBasketRuntimeApi_get_all_validator_baskets`; x = SubnetAlphaIn).
- The balancer pool weights are w = 0.5 on every subnet, so a one-shot sale cuts the price by 1 − (x/(x+E))².
- I checked this against `SwapRuntimeApi_sim_swap_alpha_for_tao(netuid, E)`.

  | SN92 | 49,063 | 11.2% | 19.1% | 55 funds, largest single fund holding 11,689 α; E/AlphaOut 7.8%; spot 65.7 τ, sim sale 59.0 τ (89.9% average fill) |
  | SN103 | 70,972 | 22.5% | 33.4% | |
  | SN70 | 57,665 | 26.4% | 37.4% | |
  | SN36 | 38,019 | 24.0% | 34.9% | |

  | SN76 | 31,907 | 34.8% | 45.0% | |
  | SN108 | 6,328 | 9.1% | 16.1% | |
  | SN40 | 47,074 | 7.7% | 13.8% | |
  | SN122 | 42,763 | 12.9% | 21.5% | |
  | SN116 | 8,316 | 15.9% | 25.7% | |
  | SN58 | 50,427 | 43.0% | 51.1% | |
  | SN90 | 57,483 | 30.0% | 40.9% | |
  | SN84 | 21,718 | 3.5% | 6.7% | old, low RootProp |

- Your SN92 estimate of about 9×10⁴ α was cumulative gross inflow. That is roughly right (about 475k blocks × 0.18–0.20 α/block), but about 40–45% of it has already been released or was redeployed during the curated window. A sale of what is actually held would cut the price by about 19%, not about 30%.

3) RELEASE CHANNELS
- **(a) Claims: the dominant channel.** Code: `claim_root.rs::root_claim_for_hotkey`.
  - Stakers must call `claim_root` or `claim_root_with_hotkey`; there has been no auto-claim since v441.
  - A claim burns the staker's owed shares and sells take = alpha × owed/P from every non-dust holding of that validator's fund. P is the fund's total outstanding shares.
  - The sale goes through the AMM fee-free (drop_fees = true), in chunks, with price_limit = min_price, i.e. no price limit. The TAO is staked to root.
  - Claims below the threshold of 500,000 rao (0.0005 τ) are skipped.
  - Observed rate: the aggregate redeemed counter went from 15,209 to 26,255 τ between blocks 9,088,500 and 9,240,000, about 526 τ/day, roughly 1.9% of NAV per day.
  - SN92: escrow grew 40,248 → 48,847 α over that span while inflow was about 0.18 α/block. That implies about 890 α/day sold, about 2% of the holding per day, or about 70% of inflow.
  - Bursts: between blocks 9,150,000 and 9,190,000, SN92 fell 46,712 → 42,685 and 4,808 τ was redeemed network-wide. That implies about 2,000 α/day sold on SN92 (about 4.5% per day). It hit every holding at once (SN103 −3.5k, SN58 −4.2k, SN90 −4.9k), the signature of large pro-rata claims.
  - Steady state is E* ≈ inflow / claim rate, about 64k α for SN92 at 2%/day.
  - The largest possible single shock is one staker's slice of one fund: at most the largest fund holding (SN92: 11.7k α, about a 5% price drop if all of it were sold).
- **(b) swap_basket: bounded, small so far.** Code: `basket_trade.rs`.
  - Each leg must fill completely within 2%: a sell may not fill below 0.98 × max(slow EMA, fast EMA with a 600-block half-life, spot), and a buy may not fill above 1.02 × min of the same three. So it cannot dump a micro cap, and it cannot sell a holding whose spot is more than 2% below its monthly EMA.
  - Each fund can turn over at most 10% of NAV per day (token bucket refilling over 7,200 blocks).
  - Buys are additionally capped at 10% of x per holding and at 1/16 of fund NAV.
  - Only 13 funds have ever traded (BasketTradeBucket rows). The BasketLiquidityUsed buy flow went to mid and large caps (SN85, 54, 118, 61, 49, 110, 75, …); none of the bottom-10 micro caps received swap buys.
- **(c) Dust folding: negligible.**
  - `consolidate_dust_basket_holdings` runs on each claim and sells whole holdings whose realizable value is below RootClaimableThreshold[ROOT] (0.0005 τ).
  - The separate claim-dust skip (holding below min(1 τ, 0.1% of fund NAV), or the claimant's slice below 0.0001 τ, provided the slice is at most 0.01 τ) leaves holdings unsold, so it slightly slows release.
  - Queue credits from dissolved subnets, or from hotkeys no longer on root, are recycled, not sold.
- **(d) Dissolution: one-shot and first in line.** Code: `subnets/dissolution.rs`.
  - DissolveCleanupPhase::default() = SubnetBasketHoldingsToRoot ("Phase 0"). `convert_subnet_basket_holdings_to_root` sells every fund's whole holding through the AMM (fee-free, chunked, no price limit) into each fund's root cash slot.
  - This happens before AlphaInOutStakesSettleStakes divides the remaining SubnetTAO pot pro rata (`remove_stake.rs::destroy_alpha_in_out_stakes*`).
  - For subnets registered after TaoInRefundDeploymentBlock = 8,334,450, SubnetAlphaIn is counted in the payout denominator D = SubnetAlphaIn + staked alpha + SubnetProtocolAlpha.
  - The escrow then takes y·E/(x+E), where y is the pool's TAO. Each remaining holder gets y·x/((x+E)·D) per α, which is x/(x+E) of a pro-rata settlement.
  - SN92 example: y = 585 τ, the escrow takes 59.0 τ (10.1% of the pot), and holders take a 10.1% haircut, ending at about 0.00047–0.00049 τ/α against spot 0.00134 (about 35–37% of spot).
  - Haircut for the others: SN103 18.4%, SN70 20.9%, SN76 25.8%, SN58 30.1%.
  - Legacy subnets use D = staked alpha + protocol alpha instead.
  - NetworkImmunityPeriod is 864,000 blocks.

4) WORKAROUND / MONITORING
Each epoch, call `BetaBasketRuntimeApi_get_all_validator_baskets`; the lighter alternative is `StakeInfoRuntimeApi_get_stake_info_for_coldkey(escrow)`. From it compute, per subnet:
- E and E/x;
- the one-shot drop 1 − (x/(x+E))^(1/w2), with w2 = y/(y + p·x);
- the dissolution haircut E/(x+E);
- days of inflow held, E / (RootAlphaDividendsPerSubnet sum / (tempo+1) × 7200).

Model the release as dE/dt = inflow − c·E − swaps, with c fitted from the change in BasketRedeemedTao relative to NAV (about 0.02/day, with spikes up to 0.045).

Also:
- Subscribe to the BasketClaimed, BasketSwapped, BasketHoldingConverted, BasketAlphaWrittenOff, BasketDeposited, BasketStakedIn and BasketClaimDustSkipped events.
- Watch `get_subnet_to_prune` and the Σ EMA root sell flag.
- For history, Taostats has GET /api/dtao/validator/basket/history/v1 (hotkey, day_start, day_end; needs an API key).

gapfill.question: For the swap-v3 era (lazy per-subnet init from about July 2025 until the Balancer migration at block 8,486,594 on 2026-06-25), which price series and which fill/slippage model are correct, especially for small pools that had user concentrated liquidity before LP was disabled (about 2025-12-05)?
gapfill.answer:
SHORT ANSWER (verified against source code and live archive reads, as of 2026-10-08)
- Price: use P = AlphaSqrtPrice². SubnetTAO/SubnetAlphaIn (T/A) is only bookkeeping in this era.
- Fills: use a constant product on VIRTUAL reserves built from CurrentLiquidity (L), not on (SubnetTAO, SubnetAlphaIn). Equivalently, use sim_swap at the block hash.
- Cause of the tail gaps: user concentrated liquidity did NOT cause them. The cause is a single runtime change: protocol swap fees were compounded into L and never credited to SubnetTAO/SubnetAlphaIn.
- Your proposed fix is correct, with one gap in API coverage and some rate-limit problems (both below).

1) ERA BOUNDARIES (runtime version read on-chain; state_getRuntimeVersion flips at the setCode block, and the new code runs from the next block)
- v3 swap live on mainnet: the spec-290 code was set at block 5,947,548 (2025-07-08), so v3 runs from block 5,947,549. Spec 283/285 never ran on mainnet.
  - All 128 subnets had SwapV3Initialized = true by block 6.0M. There was no init migration; init is lazy and happens inside swap_inner / add_liquidity via maybe_initialize_v3.
- sim_swap API: spec 302 first appears at block 6,262,253 (about 2025-08-20).
- disable_lp extrinsic exists: spec 350 from block 7,034,932.
- Swap fees to block author: spec 391 from block 7,782,857 (about 2026-03-20). Spec 377 ran until then; the Balancer attempt in spec 380 and spec 385 were never deployed.
- Balancer: spec 423 code set at 8,486,593; migrate_swapv3_to_balancer runs at 8,486,594.
- The repo has moved: opentensor/subtensor now redirects to RaoFoundation/subtensor.

2) PRICE SERIES
- Code: pallets/swap/src/pallet/impls.rs::current_price is identical from spec 290 through 422:
  - if SwapV3Initialized(netuid): P = AlphaSqrtPrice², where AlphaSqrtPrice is a U64F64 stored as u128 LE, divided by 2^64 (TAO per alpha).
  - otherwise: P = (SubnetTAO + SubnetTaoProvided) / (SubnetAlphaIn + SubnetAlphaInProvided).
- SwapRuntimeApi_current_alpha_price(netuid: u16) -> u64 returns floor(P·1e9).
- The chain itself uses this P for:
  - emission split (run_coinbase price_i, so tao_in/alpha_in are proportional to P);
  - the SubnetMovingPrice EMA (update_moving_price);
  - stake-transfer TAO equivalents;
  - the Balancer initial price (the migration sets price = AlphaSqrtPrice², with weight w_quote = T/(P·A + T)).
- So the P series is continuous across 8,486,594. The depth is not: Balancer uses the real (T, A) reserves instead of L, so SN103 loses about 10% of its depth at the switch.

3) ROOT CAUSE OF THE T/A vs P GAP (found and dated)
- Spec 301 (v3.2.4, PR #1934 "Collect protocol fees on emissions") added position.collect_fees() to adjust_protocol_liquidity. From then on, the protocol position's swap fees were folded into L at every coinbase injection.
- SubnetTAO only ever receives amount_paid_in (fee excluded) plus injections, so the fees never reach the bookkeeping reserves.
- The first block under 301 was 6,205,195 (2025-08-12 16:39:48 UTC). In that one block, with T, A and P unchanged, L jumped on all 128 subnets by the fees accrued since July (when the default fee was 0.3%):
  - median +0.18%, p90 +2.5%, 22 subnets above +1%;
  - SN103 +71.0%, SN99 +67.6%, SN102 +23%, SN120 +17.3%, SN125 +17.3%, SN128 +9.7%, SN89 +7.2%.
- Before this event (block 6.0M): max |T/A ÷ P − 1| was 0.45% and L/sqrt(T·A) was at most 1.006.
- Compounding continued every block until spec 391. After that, the excess only dilutes.
- Mechanism: write x_v = L√P = T + a and y_v = L/√P = A + b, with a/b ≈ P0 (the price when fees were folded in). Then T/A − P has the sign of (P − P0) and grows with the price move since folding. The gap is path-dependent bias, not noise, and it is largest in small, high-churn pools: exactly your size and momentum tail.

| 6.5M | 1.002 | 1.299 (SN103) | |
| 7.5M | | 1.137 | 16.0% |
| 8.3M | | 1.102 | 10.6% |

  - SubnetTaoProvided and SubnetAlphaInProvided were 0 everywhere at 6.5M, because swaps drain the Provided buckets first.

4) FILL MODEL
Exact whenever no tick is crossed, which is the practical case. Verified against on-chain sim_swap:
- SN103, SN99 and SN104 at 6.5M: buys of 1–1000 TAO and sells worth about 10–100 TAO.
- SN103 and SN104 at 8.3M: buys of 1–100 TAO; SN103 also sold 2.5k–250k alpha.
- Model error was 0.00000–0.00003%. A constant product on T/A was off by −15.75% to +10.6%.

Formula:
- Inputs:
  - L = Swap.CurrentLiquidity (u64);
  - √P = Swap.AlphaSqrtPrice / 2^64;
  - x_v = L·√P (rao TAO);
  - y_v = L/√P (rao alpha);
  - f = Swap.FeeRate(netuid) / 65535. The default is 33 (0.0504%). It was 196 (0.299%) for specs 290–292, until block ≤6.1M. Root or the subnet owner can set it up to SwapMaxFeeRate = 10000 (15.26%); for example SN104 was 222 at 6.0M and 333 at 6.5M.
- Buy τ: fee = floor(τ·f); d = τ − fee; α_out = y_v·d / (x_v + d); new √P' = √P + d/L.
- Sell α: fee = floor(α·f); d = α − fee; τ_out = x_v·d / (y_v + d); new 1/√P' = 1/√P + d/L.
- When a step stops at a limit or edge, the fee is recomputed as δ·f/(1 − f).
- With tick crossings, use the tick walk in swap_step.rs. Ticks are 1.0001^i, with TickIndex in ±443636. Data: Swap.Ticks{liquidity_net i128, liquidity_gross u64, fees_out…}, TickIndexBitmapWords, CurrentTick.

Where fees went:

| Specs | Blocks | Fee destination |
|---|---|---|
| 290–300 | | In-range positions via FeeGlobalTao/Alpha. The protocol share accrued but was not compounded. |
| 301–377 | | The protocol share was compounded into L at each injection. |
| 391–422 | 7,782,857–8,486,593 | DefaultFeeSplit = Perbill::zero(), so 100% to the block author. |

- Under specs 391–422:
  - On a buy, the TAO fee is transferred to the author and never enters the pool.
  - On a sell, the alpha fee is sold fee-less into the same pool right after the user's swap, and the TAO goes to the author (burned if there is no author). The post-trade price therefore reflects the full alpha amount.
- Subnet-to-subnet move_stake charges only one fee leg (drop_fee_destination = origin != ROOT).

5) HISTORICAL RUNTIME API (state_call at a block hash runs that block's runtime code)
- current_alpha_price(netuid: u16) -> u64 covers the whole v3 era.
- sim_swap_tao_for_alpha(netuid: u16, tao: u64) and sim_swap_alpha_for_tao(netuid: u16, alpha: u64) -> SimSwapResult, from hash 6,262,253:
  - Specs 302–377: 4×u64 = 32 bytes {tao_amount, alpha_amount, tao_fee, alpha_fee}.
  - Specs 391 and later: 48 bytes, adding {tao_slippage, alpha_slippage}.
  - Buy: tao_amount = paid_in excluding fee, alpha_amount = output. Sell: tao_amount = output, alpha_amount = paid_in excluding fee. On error, all fields are 0.
- current_alpha_price_all() is available from spec 391.
- sim runs the same do_swap path with rollback, drop_fees = false and the default min/max price limits. Differences from a real trade:
  - It skips the reserve-overuse check (a real swap fails with InsufficientLiquidity).
  - It excludes the extrinsic fee.
  - It sees the post-state of block H, before block H+1's injection or any excess-TAO buyback.
- Gap: blocks 5,947,549–6,262,252 have no sim API. Use the formula from section 4, which is exact there, and before 6,205,195 even the T/A constant product is within about 0.5%.
- Python SDK (bittensor 10.5.0): get_subnet_price(netuid, block) and sim_swap(origin_netuid, destination_netuid, amount, block) wrap these calls. Its subnet-to-subnet sim adds two fee legs, while on-chain moves pay one.

gapfill.question: How much lead time and exit buffer does a holder get before a subnet is pruned or has its emission switched off? This covers exact prune blocks for the ~52 events, the EMA rank path and registration cost before each, whether a pruning register_network can be MEV-shielded, and how fast a subnet k ranks above the bottom can become the target given the ~8h EMA half-life.
gapfill.answer:
SHORT ANSWER
- Mempool warning is zero. A pruning registration can be MEV-shielded, and 6 of the last 10 prunes were. The subnet is removed in the same block as the registration (NetworksAdded is removed and NetworkRemoved fires). From then on remove_stake and move_stake fail with SubnetNotExists.
- The only exit buffers that hold up are:
  (a) A hard 14,400-block (~48h) window after every subnet registration, during which no prune is possible (barring a root dissolve).
  (b) The public, deterministic target and cost state, which a bot can read every block.
- Historically, the pruned subnet had been rank 1 for less than 24h in 12 of 52 cases (23%), less than 12h in 4 cases, and less than 1h in 1 case. Emission switch-offs have no on-chain lead at all.

1) RULES IN CODE
Source: github.com/opentensor/subtensor now redirects to RaoFoundation/subtensor (main, spec 476). Mainnet runs spec 475 at block 9,240,878 (2026-10-08 20:58 UTC). The rule below picked the actual pruned subnet in 52 of 52 historical events.

- Prune target. get_network_to_prune() in coinbase/root.rs:
  - Takes the minimum SubnetMovingPrice over subnets with NetworksAdded set, excluding root.
  - Skips a subnet if current_block < NetworkRegisteredAt + NetworkImmunityPeriod. On-chain NetworkImmunityPeriod is 864,000 blocks.
  - Ties go to the earliest NetworkRegisteredAt.
  - It runs only inside do_register_network (subnets/subnet.rs), and only when non-root subnets plus DissolveCleanupQueue.len() >= SubnetLimit (128).
  - If cleanup_queue_len > registration_queue_len, the registration waits instead of pruning (for example after root_dissolve_network).
- Same-block removal. do_dissolve_network (subnets/dissolution.rs) does NetworksAdded::remove, emits NetworkRemoved and pushes the subnet to DissolveCleanupQueue. The registration is then queued (NetworkRegistrationQueued, escrowed lock). NetworkAdded follows when on_idle processes the queue. Observed gap: 17–25 blocks.
- Rate limit is global, not per coldkey.
  - TransactionType::RegisterNetwork.last_block() is the global LastRateLimitedBlock(RateLimitKey::NetworkLastRegistered), storage key suffix 0x02.
  - A registration passes iff block - last >= NetworkRateLimit. On-chain NetworkRateLimit is 14,400; it was 28,800 until about Dec 2025.
  - The bittensor.com/docs catalog says "rate-limited per coldkey". The code contradicts that.
- Lock cost. get_network_lock_cost = max(NetworkMinLockCost, 2L - (L / I_eff) * (now - last_lock_block)).
  - I_eff = NetworkLockReductionInterval x calculate_block_emission/1e9 = 115,200 x 0.5 = 57,600 blocks.
  - NetworkMinLockCost = 1e9 rao (1 TAO).
  - So cost = 1.75L at rate-limit expiry and reaches 1 TAO about 115,200 blocks (16.0 days) after the last lock.
  - Now: L = 653.02 TAO, last lock at block 9,210,610, subnetInfo_getLockCost = 962.89 TAO.
- EMA update (staking/stake_utils.rs, update_moving_price):
  - alpha = SubnetMovingAlpha x b/(b + EMAPriceHalvingBlocks).
  - E <- alpha x min(spot, 1) + (1 - alpha) x E.
  - b = blocks since start_call, not since registration.
  - On-chain SubnetMovingAlpha = 0.0003 (raw I96F32 1,288,490; the code default is 0.000003). EMAPriceHalvingBlocks = 201,600 for every subnet.
  - Half-life = ln2/alpha:
    - About 8.1h for genesis-era subnets (alpha ≈ 0.000286).
    - 9.4h for SN92.
    - 14.9h at 30 days after start_call.
    - 1.6 days at 7 days after start_call.
    - 9.3 days at 1 day after start_call.
  - The EMA is updated in on_initialize (block_step, after run_coinbase) only for get_subnets_to_emit_to: FirstEmissionBlockNumber set, SubtokenEnabled, and NetworkRegistrationAllowed. So the target for block N is fixed before any extrinsic in block N.
  - Never-started subnets keep EMA exactly 0.
  - SubnetEmissionEnabled = false does NOT freeze the EMA. NetworkRegistrationAllowed = false does.
  - After start_call, the EMA ramps as E/s ≈ 1 - exp(-0.0003 x (b - 201,600 x ln(1 + b/201,600))): about 4% after 1 day, 28% after 3 days, 80% after 7 days.
- MEV shield:
  - pallet_shield::submit_encrypted (MevShield index 30, call 1) takes any signed extrinsic encrypted with ML-KEM-768 and XChaCha20-Poly1305.
  - The node's block proposer (RaoFoundation/polkadot-sdk basic_authorship) pushes the wrapper and the decrypted inner transaction into the same block.
  - There is no call filter. The extension only checks ciphertext format, and BaseCallFilter = SafeMode ∩ NoNestingCallFilter.
  - The store_encrypted path is inert on mainnet (ExtrinsicDecryptor = ()).
  - SDK 10.5.0 register_subnet_extrinsic(mev_protection=...) supports shielding; it is off unless the BT_MEV_PROTECTION environment variable is set.
  - The mempool shows only a ~1.4 KB submit_encrypted from the signer's coldkey.
- Emission flag. sudo_set_subnet_emission_enabled (AdminUtils call 94) requires ensure_root.
  - It zeroes the subnet's TAO-side share (alpha_out continues). The share is redistributed to enabled subnets.
  - New subnets start with the flag set to false.

gapfill.question: On the production path (Staking proxy, then MevShield submit_shielded/submit_encrypted, then AddStakeLimit/RemoveStakeLimit), what are the measured inclusion rate, blocks of latency, expiry rate inside the 8-block era, PriceLimitExceeded and SlippageTooHigh frequency, and all-in fee (inner call plus the Proxy.proxy wrapper plus the MevShield carrier) after the spec-467 fee halving?
gapfill.answer:
SHORT ANSWER
Public chain data answers 4 of the 5 numbers: latency, decrypt/execute rate, the two limit-error rates, and the all-in fee. Expiry and never-included carriers leave no trace on chain, so you can only measure those from your own submit logs. The code fixes the mechanics, though: a carrier can be decrypted in exactly one block, N+2.

1) HOW IT WORKS (from the code; chain spec 475 measured live on 2026-10-08, main branch spec_version 476)
- SDK `client.submit_shielded()` maps to the chain call `MevShield.submit_encrypted(ciphertext ≤8192 B)` (pallet 30, call 1).
- The inner call is the already-composed `Proxy.proxy(real, force_proxy_type, call)`. It is signed at nonce+1 and encrypted to `MevShield.NextKey`, which is the ML-KEM-768 key of the author at slot+2. The carrier is signed at nonce.
- Both use the SDK default `MEV_SHIELD_ERA_PERIOD=8`. The runtime rejects carriers with an era longer than 8 (`MAX_SHIELD_ERA_PERIOD=8`, error `InvalidTransaction::Stale`).
- The SDK anchors the mortal era at the FINALIZED head (`_normalize_era`), not the best head.
- Proposer logic (RaoFoundation/polkadot-sdk basic_authorship.rs):
  - A carrier is pushed only if `key_hash == twox128(PendingKey at the parent block)`. Otherwise it is skipped and left in the pool, not marked invalid.
  - After pushing the carrier, the proposer decrypts it and pushes the inner extrinsic directly after it, in the same block.
  - If decryption fails or the inner extrinsic is invalid, it is silently dropped. The carrier fee is still charged.
- Consequences:
  - Inclusion happens at block N+2, where N is the head at which you read NextKey. That gives a 12–24 s submit window (`NextKeyExpiresAt = now+3`, exclusive).
  - A carrier that misses N+2 can never be decrypted later. It sits in the pool until its era expires.
  - An Aura slot skipped at s+1 or s+2 shifts the PendingKey pipeline. The next author then includes the carrier but cannot decrypt it: you pay the fee and nothing executes. This is from code reading only and never happened in my sample.
  - `store_encrypted` is not the production path (the runtime sets `ExtrinsicDecryptor = ()`).
  - Transaction priority is flat (Normal class = 1), so tips buy nothing.

2) WHAT I MEASURED ON MAINNET
Two windows at spec 475:
- W1: blocks 9,239,851–9,240,850
- W2: blocks 9,236,200–9,237,399

Method: decoded every block body and its System.Events. An inner extrinsic is paired with its carrier when it is the next extrinsic (index+1) and its length equals `ct_len − 1146` (16+2+1088+24+16 bytes).

- **Carriers included:** 2,673 from 263+ distinct signers, about 1.2 per block.
- **Inner decrypted and included in the same block:** 2,644/2,673 = 98.9%.
  - W1: 98.1% (27 missing). At least 10 of the 12 missing carriers I inspected came from one non-SDK cohort that tips 0.01–0.02 TAO and signs one block before inclusion.
  - W2: 99.84% (2 missing).
  - Excluding that cohort: about 99.4% or better.
  - 100% of paired inners sat in the carrier's own block.
- **Latency:** from era birth to inclusion the distribution was 1:9, 2:78, 3:362, 4:1931, 5:293 blocks (n=2,673). The maximum was 5. That fits N+2 targeting plus about 2 blocks of GRANDPA lag in the finalized anchor. From submission, it is 1–2 blocks (12–24 s).
- **Missed Aura slots:** 0 in 14,400 consecutive blocks (9,226,400–9,240,800). The 95% upper bound is about 0.02% per slot, so the missed-slot failure path is currently below about 0.04% per order.
- **Expiry or never-included rate:** cannot be determined from chain data. Expected to be well under 1% for a hot-key bot that reads NextKey from a node at the network head and submits within about 1 s. This is an engineering estimate.
- **Outcomes of the 2,644 executed inners:**
  - SlippageTooHigh: 38 (1.44%)
  - PriceLimitExceeded: 18 (0.68%)
  - NotEnoughBalanceToStake: 39
  - AmountTooLow: 98 (mostly one bot)
- **Single-leaf limit orders, direct plus proxied:**

| Call | n | SlippageTooHigh | PriceLimitExceeded |
|---|---|---|---|
| add_stake_limit | 514 | 8 (1.6%) | 6 (1.2%) |
| remove_stake_limit | 458 | 3 (0.7%) | 4 (0.9%) |
| remove_stake_full_limit | 166 | 5 (3.0%) | — |
| Proxied add_stake_limit only (small n) | 40 | 1 (2.5%) | 3 (7.5%) |

- **For comparison, unshielded add_stake_limit in W1 (n=134):** PriceLimitExceeded 11.9%, SlippageTooHigh 6.7%. These are different trader populations, so treat it as observational only.
- **Shielded proxied calls work end to end.** I saw shielded `Proxy(add_stake_limit)`, `Proxy(add_stake)`, `Proxy(remove_stake_full_limit)` and `Proxy(force_batch[...])` execute.
  - Proxied inner errors appear as `Proxy.ProxyExecuted{result: Err}` under an `ExtrinsicSuccess`, so reconcile on ProxyExecuted, not on ExtrinsicSuccess.
  - `PriceLimitExceeded` is raised by the swap pallet before the trade is checked: `ensure!(order.is_beyond_price_limit(current_price, limit))` runs inside `get_max_amount_add`. A limit that is already crossed therefore fails even with `allow_partial=true`.
  - `SlippageTooHigh` only happens with `allow_partial=false` and `amount > max_amount`.

3) FEES AFTER THE SPEC-467 HALVING
Source: pallets/transaction-fee/src/lib.rs.
- `WEIGHT_FEE_PER_REF_TIME = Perbill(250_000)`, i.e. 0.00025 rao per unit of ref_time (was 0.0005).
- `LENGTH_FEE_PER_BYTE = Perbill(500_000_000)`, i.e. 0.5 rao/byte (was 1).
- fee = base (about 27,039 rao) + 0.5·len + 0.00025·weight. Some calls are also capped at their spec-459 weight (staking_fee.rs).
- The fee multiplier is constant (1). The carrier fee is always paid in TAO by the carrier signer.
- The inner fee is paid by the delegate, unless the real account has opted in with `Proxy.set_real_pays_fee(delegate, true)`.

Measured `TransactionFeePaid.actual_fee` values, excluding tips:

| Call | Measured (rao) | Quote (rao) |
|---|---|---|
| Carrier | p50 94,554–94,566, range 94,543–95,223 (≈τ0.0000946) | live `query_call_info` 94,576 at 1,346 B; `estimate_shielded_carrier_fee` (8192-B worst case) 98,000 |
| Proxy(add_stake_limit) | 933,081 (n=22) | 948,083 = 27,039 base + 100 length + 920,944 weight |
| add_stake_limit (direct) | 850,536 | 850,506 at 100 B, matches `fee_baseline/pins.tsv` |
| remove_stake_limit (direct) | 645,119 | — |
| Proxy(remove_stake_limit) | — | 742,666 |
| Proxy(remove_stake_full_limit) | 749,660 | — |
| swap_stake_limit | 1,069,370 | — |

The proxy wrapper adds about 82.5k–97.5k rao after post-dispatch refund.

All-in per order:
- **Buy:** about 1,028k rao ≈ τ0.00103. `plan()` fee + carrier estimate gives a conservative ≈ τ0.00105.
- **Sell:** about 822k–837k rao ≈ τ0.00083.
- **Round trip:** ≈ τ0.00186.
- **Swap fee:** add `FeeRate/65535` per pool leg on the input side. All 129 subnets are at the default 33, i.e. 0.0504%; only 1 storage entry exists and it equals the default.
- **Failed inner calls pay the full fee.** add_stake_limit returns DispatchResult, so there is no refund.

Cost relative to a buy leg: 1.03% at 0.1 TAO, 0.41% at 0.25, 0.21% at 0.5, 0.10% at 1 TAO. The shield is only about 9% of that cost; the stake call's weight fee is about 80%.

Cheaper alternatives:
- `Proxy(swap_stake_limit)` for an A→B rotation: ≈ 94.6k + 1,069k + about 90k ≈ τ0.00125, versus τ0.00186 for a separate sell plus buy (it pays 2 swap fees).
- Dropping the shield below about 1 TAO saves τ0.0000946. The docs (money.mdx) say small swaps "well under ~1 TAO" are unattractive front-running targets.

The SDK comment "typical fees are ~τ0.000125" in intents/staking.py is wrong for staking calls. `_ALL_STAKE_FEE_HEADROOM_RAO = 500_000` is below the actual add_stake fee, which makes `amount='all'` buys fragile.

4) ENGINEERING WORKAROUND FOR THE PARTS YOU CANNOT MEASURE
Log your own submissions:
- Record head N when reading NextKey, NextKeyExpiresAt, the carrier hash, `inner_extrinsic_hash`, and the nonce.
- At block N+2, a missing carrier means a miss. It is final: it cannot land decryptably later.
- Otherwise check that the inner is at carrier index+1, then read ExtrinsicFailed / ProxyExecuted / ItemFailed.

Operating rules:
- Read NextKey and the best head from the same node, and refuse to submit if that node lags the network.
- After a miss, the stale carrier holds nonce n until its era expires. Flat priority blocks same-nonce replacement, and `accountNextIndex` would put the next order on a nonce gap. So either wait for era expiry (about 6 blocks) or rotate across 2–3 funded Staking-proxy delegates.

Paper-trading model:
- Execution happens at N+2, about 24 s after the quote.
- P(decrypt and include | landed) ≈ 0.99–0.998.
- Apply a deterministic AMM check for PriceLimitExceeded/SlippageTooHigh against the pool at N+2.
- Charge fees on every attempt.

Tiny mainnet probes and test.finney dry runs were not done; they need your explicit approval.

gapfill.question: Which historical data source can supply ~20 months of block- or hourly-level pool state together with SubnetMovingPrice, MinerBurned, SubnetEmissionEnabled, EmissionGateBar, RootProp and per-hotkey share state, at acceptable cost and terms? gapfill.answer:
SHORT ANSWER
(A) The moving-price EMA did not change around January 2026. The code, the parameters and the observed per-block behaviour all match the same formula from Nov 2025 to Oct 2026. The SubnetEdge claim that reaction time went from about 10h to about 48h is not reflected on chain.
(B) Only an archive JSON-RPC node holds every series you listed. The cheapest workable source is the OnFinality Bittensor archive endpoint, queried with state_queryStorageAt (many keys in one call). The free public URL works, and a free Developer key gives more headroom. Taostats cannot supply MinerBurned, EmissionGateBar or a clean SubnetMovingPrice series. Its pool history also has no field that tells netuid generations apart. Use it only for cross-checks and for trade/volume convenience. Run your own archive node only if you need every block for every subnet.

=== PART A: EMA FORMULA (as of 2026-10-08) ===
Code (pallets/subtensor/src/staking/stake_utils.rs::update_moving_price, RaoFoundation/subtensor main; github.com/opentensor/subtensor now 301-redirects there):
  b_n = n - (FirstEmissionBlockNumber(netuid) - 1)
  a_n = SubnetMovingAlpha * b_n / (b_n + H),  H = EMAPriceHalvingBlocks(netuid), default T::InitialEmaPriceHalvingPeriod = 201_600 (4 weeks)
  M_n = (1 - a_n)*M_{n-1} + a_n*min(P_spot, 1.0)
- SubnetMovingAlpha on chain is I96F32 raw 0x13A92A, which is 0.00029999995604. The code default is 0.000003.
- The update runs once per block in block_step, after run_coinbase, so emission in block n uses M_{n-1}.
- Only subnets returned by get_subnets_to_emit_to are updated. That means: not root, FirstEmissionBlockNumber set, SubtokenEnabled, and registration allowed (the last two filters were added on 2025-11-08, commit 8b8f763a). Any other subnet's EMA stays frozen.
- get_moving_alpha_price returns 1.0 for root and for mechanism-0 subnets.

Code history: I hashed the function body at commits from Jun 2025, Aug 2025, Oct 2025, Dec 2025, Jan 6 2026, Feb 2026, Mar 2026, Aug 2026 and Sep 2026. Only these changes appear:
1. get_alpha_price became SwapInterface::current_alpha_price in mid-2025 (swap v3).
2. The fixed-point type changed from U96F32 to U64F64 in release-root-reborn (2026-08-03). This affects precision only.
3. Sep 2026 added update_fast_moving_price: SubnetFastMovingPrice, half-life BASKET_FAST_EMA_HALF_LIFE_BLOCKS = 600, not clamped. It is used only for swap_basket bounds, not for emission.
4. On 2025-11-06 (commit 8ad48b37) the call moved from run_coinbase to block_step. Cadence and subnet set stayed the same.
There is no Jan 2026 commit to the function, to DefaultMovingAlpha or to InitialEmaPriceHalvingPeriod. The Jan 2026 commits to stake_utils.rs were the taoflow root-claim hotfix (spec 366), SafeFloat and bigmath work, and a lazy migration.

On-chain check (OnFinality and opentensor archives). I computed a_obs = (M_n - M_{n-1}) / (min(P_{n-1},1) - M_{n-1}), with P from SwapRuntimeApi_current_alpha_price at block n-1, and compared it with the formula's value (a_exp):

Subnet 100 is a young subnet (FirstEmissionBlockNumber 6,902,729), so it is the case most sensitive to H. EMAPriceHalvingBlocks was unset, meaning 201,600, at every sample. SubnetMovingAlpha read bit-identical 0.0003 at every sample. The runtime was spec 367 from Jan 11 to Jan 25, so no runtime upgrade landed near 2026-01-15.

Reaction times implied by the formula:
- Mature subnet (b much larger than H): half-life = ln2/0.0003, about 2,310 blocks or 7.7h. With b/(b+H) around 0.9 this is about 8.1–8.4h, which is roughly the "~10h" in the post.

=== PART B: DATA SOURCE ===
Regime boundaries verified by archive binary search:
- RootProp: first entry at block 7,135,420 (2025-12-19, spec 365).
- SubnetEmissionEnabled: Taostats says the switch exists from spec 411 (block 8,283,784). The first explicit entry is at 8,294,730 (2026-05-30). Before that the switch did not exist, so treat every subnet as enabled; an absent key later means the code default, true.
- Flow-to-price emission shares: the last SubnetEmaTaoFlow update is at block 8,466,530 (2026-06-23 01:25:24 UTC). The state at that block reports spec 421 (spec 419 at 8,466,529), so the first block run under spec 421 is 8,466,531. get_shares_flow is now dead code.

- Shares: get_shares = normalise(SubnetMovingPrice), multiply by (1 - MinerBurned), renormalise, apply the gate. Disabled subnets get 0 and their share goes to the others.
- Prune (get_network_to_prune): the lowest SubnetMovingPrice among subnets where block >= NetworkRegisteredAt + NetworkImmunityPeriod. A tie goes to the earliest registered subnet.

- /v1/subnets/pools/history:
  - by_hour means every 300th block and by_day every 7,200th.
  - It adds subnet_emission_enabled, which is null below spec 411.
  - Pages are capped at a 1,000,000-row window; use block ranges to go deeper.
- Neither pool route has moving_price, MinerBurned, EmissionGateBar or any generation key. Rows are keyed only by (netuid, block), so a reused netuid's series runs straight through dissolution and re-registration. I inferred this from the schema; I did not pull data, because that needs an account.
- Split generations with /api/subnet/registration/v1, or with registered_at_block from /api/subnet/pruning/history/v1, or with on-chain NetworkRegisteredAt.
- moving_price appears only in pruning history, whose sampling cadence is undocumented. hotkey_alpha_shares/history gives alpha and shares, also with undocumented cadence.
- Terms (updated 2026-10-06): no reselling API data without written consent; you must respect rate limits.
- There is also a WebSocket RPC proxy at /v1/rpc/ws/finney_archive. Its credit cost is unknown.

Own archive node: at least about 3.5 TB of NVMe, 16 GB+ RAM, and an initial sync of several days (official running-a-node guide). It is the only option that is practical for block-level data on every subnet and many hotkeys.

RECOMMENDED PIPELINE
1. Snapshot on chain every 60 blocks, i.e. blocks where n % 60 == 0. This is a multiple of both Taostats' 300-block hour and the 360-block gate cadence.
   - Each snapshot is one chain_getBlockHash call plus one state_queryStorageAt call of up to about 2,300 keys:
     - per subnet: SubnetTAO, SubnetAlphaIn, SubnetAlphaOut, SubnetMovingPrice, SubnetVolume, RootProp, MinerBurned, SubnetEmissionEnabled, FirstEmissionBlockNumber, NetworkRegisteredAt, SubnetOwner, SubtokenEnabled, NetworkRegistrationAllowed, EMAPriceHalvingBlocks, SubnetMechanism, SubnetTaoFlow, SubnetEmaTaoFlow, SubnetProtocolAlpha
     - globals: SubnetMovingAlpha, EmissionGateBar, EmissionBarQuantile, EmissionBarRank, EmissionGateExponent, TaoWeight, SubnetLimit, NetworkRateLimit, NetworkImmunityPeriod
   - Add a second call for chosen hotkeys: TotalHotkeyAlpha, TotalHotkeySharesV2 and legacy TotalHotkeyShares.
   - From dTAO launch (about block 4.92M) to 9.24M that is about 72k snapshots and about 144k RU. That is under half a day of the free OnFinality key, or about 12h on the public URL at the measured 1.7 snapshots/s. Every 300 blocks is about 14.4k snapshots, about 2.4h.
2. Fill in absent ValueQuery keys with the defaults from state_getMetadata at that block's runtime, cached per spec version. Defaults change between runtimes; for example EmissionBarRank.
3. Between snapshots, rebuild M_n with the verified formula, or simply interpolate: with a half-life of 8h or more and 60-block sampling, the error is negligible.
4. Do not dump the whole per-hotkey state each hour. At head there are at least 40k TotalHotkeyAlpha keys and at least 30k AlphaV2 keys (both counts capped). Track only the relevant hotkeys.
5. Use Taostats only as an independent check of price and reserves at block % 300 == 0, and for trades and volume. Volume can also come from differencing the on-chain SubnetVolume counter.

gapfill.caveats:
- Throughput figures come from one IP on one day (2026-10-08) and may change. OnFinality's own documents disagree: the Bittensor page says 5 req/s, while the generic HTTP default is 3,000 RU/min. The opentensor archive's limit is undocumented apart from "~1 req/s".
- Taostats credit cost per endpoint is not published, and the tier gating of individual endpoints cannot be read from the OpenAPI specs. The cost estimates assume 1 credit per call, which is unverified.
- I did not create a Taostats account, so I could not pull data. The claim that generation rows mix is inferred from the schema; the response has no generation field.
- Runtime defaults for absent storage keys differ by spec version, so resolve them from historical metadata. Example: at the first gate block (spec 440), EmissionBarRank and EmissionBarQuantile were both unset, and their defaults at that runtime may differ from today's code (rank 32, q 0.61).
- I did not pin the exact on-chain block where the fixed-point type changed from U96F32 to U64F64 (release-root-reborn, merged 2026-08-03). It affects precision only.
- The "legacy Alpha fully drained" block came from a binary search that assumes the drain was monotonic.
- My on-chain SubnetMovingAlpha samples (Nov 2025 and Jan–Oct 2026) do not rule out a set-and-revert between samples. However, the per-block a_obs checks on both sides of 2026-01-15 match 0.0003 × b/(b+201,600) within about 1%.
- Superellipse pools (PR #3211) are mentioned in Taostats docs; I did not check whether they are live. If they are, they may change which swap-pallet state is needed to replay slippage; spot price through the runtime API is unaffected.
- I found no public docs for a tao.app API, and could not confirm archive support on Dwellir or GetBlock.
